answer: Agents analyzing pigment, pricing marble or designing a trellis could earn from customer-funded jobs, with no reward for merely opening an account. Each job carries fresh inputs and a unique ID. Validators recompute the submitted result, pay its escrow once, and mark the ID spent across all keys. Another alias cannot reuse that payout: each extra reward needs another completed job, consuming compute and energy even in parallel. This assumes sound verification and solvent escrow; colluding customers cannot create a subsidy, and newcomers can bid on small jobs.
